newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended lower but the market was seen with scope for further gains.
Prices on Friday were presssured by declines in German bonds but traders said Swiss bonds were seen cheap relative to swaps, and this helped support prices, also versus Bunds.

The market was also encouraged by speculation that the Swiss franc will stay fairly firm. Aside from reactions to the weekend's Group of Seven meeting, Swiss activity next week may focus on parliamentary discussions about a 561 million Swiss franc stimulus package. A decision on the federal package is expected by Tuesday or Wednesday.
The market's strong performance this week was highlighted by good demand for CS Group's new $1 billion Swiss franc 10-year corporate straight bond launched Wednesday.
The bond was increased from an initial 500 million francs, making it the the largest corporate straight bond ever launched in Swiss francs, dealers said.
A CSFB syndicate spokesman said that much of the demand for the new issue came from Swiss domestic investors.
"In the Swiss franc capital market, there is very good demand for domestic paper," the spokesman said.
He said the issue was aimed especially at domestic institutional investors seeking a four percent coupon.
The new offering's large size -- it is bigger than some tranches of Swiss Confederate bonds -- creates a liquid bond as an alternative to Swiss federal bonds.

The European Commission's review Wednesday of prospective EMU members' budget deficits was also seen positive for Swiss bonds. It showed all potential members could join the common Euro currency except Italy and Greece.
This implied to some market participants that the common currency entry criteria were being watered down.
"It all goes in the direction of a weak euro, and stronger Swiss franc, and thus lower Swiss interest rates," said Herbert Fritschi, analyst at Zurich Cantonalbank.
The Swiss National Bank has said repeatedly it would adjust policy if the franc sees unwanted appreciation linked to EMU.

Conf futures down seven at 118.99.
Comi medium-term bond down five at 111.00
Euro Swiss francs up two at 98.16.
